assumptions.text: The 800-customer target is assessed at the end of a deadline still to be confirmed; the 6–12-month expansion window is not automatically treated as that deadline.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: Avoiding monthly operating losses is a provisional reading of the concern about losing money and needs confirmation.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: Until evidence supports a different forecast, current acquisition and churn rates are held constant in the carry-on route. The customer base still changes through acquisitions and churn.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: For the initial comparison, setup investment is counted once at the start, additional monthly spending runs from the start through the comparison window, and customer effects begin only after the route's launch delay. Actual staged payment and spending schedules may differ.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: Monthly churn is treated as the share of the opening customer base lost each month, with new acquisitions added during that month.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: The initial profit calculation uses one marginal monthly profit response per additional customer, excludes separately counted expansion overhead from that response, and requires validation against the actual customer mix and service capacity.
assumptions.author: olumi

assumptions.text: For this provisional comparison, Olumi proposes treating the person's 12% monthly churn warning as a hard limit in every month of the comparison period. This interpretation awaits approval: it is not the person's instruction, and staying within it does not guarantee profitability. The existing warning and operating-profit goal remain separate and unchanged.
assumptions.author: olumi
